Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle can be understood by comparing it to taking a photograph of a fast-moving car. If you use a very fast shutter speed, the car appears sharp and you know exactly where it is at that moment (position), but the image is frozen, so you cannot tell how fast it was going (momentum). Conversely, if you use a slow shutter speed, the car appears as a blur, giving you a good sense of its speed and direction, but you lose the precise information about its exact location at any single instant. This trade-off mirrors the quantum reality that you cannot simultaneously know both the precise position and momentum of a particle.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
